facts.statement: Pachycephalosaurus was among the last non-avian dinosaurs to exist before the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.
facts.quote: It was among the last species of non-avian dinosaurs on Earth before the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event

facts.statement: Fossils of Pachycephalosaurus have been found in Montana, South Dakota, Wyoming, and Alberta.
facts.quote: Remains have been excavated in Montana, South Dakota, Wyoming, and Alberta

facts.statement: Pachycephalosaurus is estimated to have reached 4.5 meters in length and weighed between 370 and 450 kilograms.
facts.quote: Pachycephalosaurus is estimated to have reached 4.5 m long and weighed 370 - 450 kg

facts.statement: Pachycephalosaurus was a bipedal herbivore with long strong legs and small arms that had five fingers.
facts.quote: Like other pachycephalosaurids, Pachycephalosaurus was a bipedal herbivore, possessing long, strong legs and somewhat small arms with five-fingered hands

facts.statement: Pachycephalosaurus is the largest known pachycephalosaur, characterized by an extremely thick, slightly domed skull roof.
facts.quote: Pachycephalosaurus is the largest-known pachycephalosaur, known for having an extremely thick, slightly domed skull roof

facts.statement: The skull structure suggests Pachycephalosaurus used its head as a battering ram for defense or combat with other members of its species.
facts.quote: visually, the structure of the skull suggests a "battering ram" function in life, evolved for use as a defensive mechanism or intra-species combat

facts.statement: The hypothesis that Pachycephalosaurus used its skull for head-butting has been disputed in recent years.
facts.quote: This hypothesis has been disputed in recent years

facts.statement: The genus Tylosteus is considered synonymous with Pachycephalosaurus.
facts.quote: The genus Tylosteus is synonymous with Pachycephalosaurus

facts.statement: The synonymy of Stygimoloch with Pachycephalosaurus is disputed because specimens from each genus come from different time periods in rock layers.
facts.quote: The proposed synonymy for Stygimoloch with Pachycephalosaurus, however, has been disputed in recent literature due to temporal difference in the rock layers where specimens attributed to each genera have been recovered

facts.statement: The bone fragment for Tylosteus ornatus was collected by Ferdinand Vandeveer Hayden from the head of the Missouri River, with its Cretaceous age indicated the following year.
facts.quote: This bone fragment was collected by Ferdinand Vandeveer Hayden from the "head of the Missouri River", with a Cretaceous age indicated the next year

facts.statement: The bone fragment was doubtfully identified as a dinosaur by Oliver Perry Hay in 1902 and definitively identified as a dinosaur by Charles Whitney Gilmore in 1928.
facts.quote: it was doubtfully identified as a dinosaur instead by Oliver Perry Hay in 1902, and then more definitively as a dinosaur by Charles Whitney Gilmore in 1928

facts.statement: Donald Baird and John R. Horner independently identified the Tylosteus holotype ANSP 8568 as a squamosal from a Pachycephalosaurus skull.
facts.quote: Baird and John R. Horner independently came across the Tylosteus holotype ANSP 8568 in the collections of the Academy of Natural Sciences of Philadelphia and concluded that it was the squamosal from a skull of Pachycephalosaurus

facts.statement: Donald Baird suggested that Joseph Leidy's identification of the discovery location as the head of the Missouri River was a misunderstanding of the confluence of the Jefferson and Madison Rivers.
facts.quote: Baird suggested that Leidy's identification of the head of the Missouri River, commonly accepted even at the time to refer to the confluence of the Jefferson and Madison Rivers, was the result of a misunderstanding

facts.statement: In 1990, W. P. Coombs stated that a tooth collected by Hatcher came from a pachycephalosaurid, possibly Pachycephalosaurus itself.
facts.quote: In 1990, American paleontologist W. P. Coombs stated the tooth came from a pachycephalosaurid, possibly even Pachycephalosaurus itself

facts.statement: In 1986, the International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature affirmed Pachycephalosaurus as the conserved name and rejected Tylosteus.
facts.quote: Baird advocated for conserving Pachycephalosaurus and rendering Tylosteus ornatus a nomen oblitum, which was affirmed by the International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature in 1986 where Tylosteus was made a nomen rejectum and Pachycephalosaurus a nomen conservandum

facts.statement: A partial skull of Pachycephalosaurus was discovered in 1930 in the Lance Formation of Niobrara County, Wyoming.
facts.quote: In 1930, American paleontologist George Fryer Sternberg discovered a partial skull within the Lance Formation of Niobrara County, Wyoming

facts.statement: The species Pachycephalosaurus wyomingensis was named by Charles W. Gilmore in 1931.
facts.quote: P. wyomingensis, the type and currently only valid species of Pachycephalosaurus, was named by Charles W. Gilmore in 1931

facts.statement: The genus Pachycephalosaurus was established in 1943 by Barnum Brown and Erich Maren Schlaikjer.
facts.quote: In 1943, Barnum Brown and Erich Maren Schlaikjer, with newer, more complete material, established the genus Pachycephalosaurus

facts.statement: Pachycephalosaurus had a large bony dome on its skull up to 25 cm thick.
facts.quote: Pachycephalosaurus is famous for having a large, bony dome on top of its skull, up to 25 cm thick

facts.statement: Pachycephalosaurus had a short skull with large, forward-facing eye sockets suggesting binocular vision.
facts.quote: The skull was short and possessed large, rounded eye sockets that faced forward, suggesting that the animal had binocular vision

facts.statement: Pachycephalosaurus was a bipedal dinosaur and possibly the largest of all pachycephalosaurids.
facts.quote: Pachycephalosaurus was bipedal and possibly the largest of all pachycephalosaurids

facts.statement: Pachycephalosaurus was estimated to be about 4.5 meters long and weigh between 370 and 450 kg.
facts.quote: It has been estimated that Pachycephalosaurus was about 4.5 m long and weighed about 370-450 kg

facts.statement: Pachycephalosaurus is the most famous member of the clade Pachycephalosauria.
facts.quote: Pachycephalosaurus is the most famous member of Pachycephalosauria, even if it is not the best-preserved member

facts.statement: Researchers have debated whether Stygimoloch and Dracorex are distinct species or growth stages of Pachycephalosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2009, Horenr and Goodwin proposed that Stygimoloch and Dracorex represent younger growth stages of Pachycephalosaurus, and thus should be classified as junior synonyms

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest Stygimoloch might represent a different species, Pachycephalosaurus spinifer, rather than a growth stage.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul proposed that, while Stygimoloch and Dracorex possibly represent different growth stages of Pachycephalosaurus, Stygimoloch might represent a different species, P. spinifer

facts.statement: Recent studies indicate Stygimoloch may be a separate genus restricted to the uppermost Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: In 2025, Wroblewski treated Stygimoloch as a separate genus to which he attributed three specimens from the Ferris Formation, providing further evidence that this taxon was restricted to the uppermost Maastrichtian

facts.statement: In 2007, researchers proposed that Stygimoloch and Dracorex were juvenile or female forms of Pachycephalosaurus.
facts.quote: However, in 2007, they were proposed to be juvenile or female morphologies of Pachycephalosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2009, Horner and Goodwin published findings showing that skull bones of Pachycephalosaurus, Stygimoloch, and Dracorex exhibit extreme plasticity.
facts.quote: Horner and M.B. Goodwin published their findings in 2009, showing that the spike and skull dome bones of all three "species" exhibit extreme plasticity

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest Stygimoloch might be a distinct species, P. spinifer, or a separate genus rather than a juvenile Pachycephalosaurus.
facts.quote: This has also led to suggestions that Stygimoloch might represent its own species, P. spinifer, or a distinct genus.

facts.statement: A long-standing hypothesis suggests male Pachycephalosaurus engaged in head-butting similar to bighorn sheep or musk oxen.
facts.quote: It has been widely hypothesized for decades that Pachycephalosaurus and its relatives were the ancient, bipedal equivalents of bighorn sheep or musk oxen, where male individuals would ram each other headlong

facts.statement: An alternative hypothesis proposes that Pachycephalosaurus engaged in flank-butting rather than head-butting during combat.
facts.quote: Alternatively, Pachycephalosaurus and other pachycephalosaurids may have engaged in flank-butting during intraspecific combat.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Cary Woodruff suggests Pachycephalosaurus may have used 'kickboxing' behavior similar to kangaroos instead of head-butting.
facts.quote: Research headed by paleontologist Cary Woodruff noted that Pachycephalosaurus's spine, pelvis and tail share resemblances to kangaroos over headbutting animals like bighorn sheep.

facts.statement: A 2012 study indicated that cranial pathologies in a Pachycephalosaurus specimen were likely caused by agonistic behavior.
facts.quote: In 2012, a study showed that cranial pathologies in a P. wyomingensis specimen were likely due to agonistic behavior.

facts.statement: A 2013 study found that 22% of examined pachycephalosaur domes had lesions consistent with osteomyelitis, supporting the combat hypothesis.
facts.quote: Peterson et al. (2013) studied cranial pathologies among Pachycephalosauridae and found that 22% of all domes examined had lesions that are consistent with osteomyelitis

facts.statement: Histological analysis shows pachycephalosaur domes are made of fibrolamellar bone containing fibroblasts that aid in rapid wound healing.
facts.quote: Histological examination reveals that pachycephalosaurid domes are composed of a unique form of fibrolamellar bone that contains fibroblasts, which play a critical role in wound healing

facts.statement: Pachycephalosaurus had small, ridged teeth that were ineffective for chewing tough fibrous plants.
facts.quote: Having very small, ridged teeth, they could not have chewed tough, fibrous plants like flowering shrubs as effectively as other dinosaurs of the same period.

facts.statement: There is some suspicion that Pachycephalosaurus may have included meat in its diet.
facts.quote: It has also been suspected to a degree that it may have included meat in its diet.

facts.statement: Nearly all Pachycephalosaurus fossils have been found in the Lance and Hell Creek Formations of the northwestern United States.
facts.quote: Nearly all Pachycephalosaurus fossils have been recovered from the Lance Formation and Hell Creek Formation of the northwestern United States.

facts.statement: Pachycephalosaurus coexisted with diverse dinosaurs including ceratopsians, hadrosaurs, ankylosaurs, and theropods like Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Other dinosaurs that shared its time and place include Thescelosaurus, the hadrosaurid Edmontosaurus and possibly Parasaurolophus, ceratopsians like Triceratops, Torosaurus, Nedoceratops, Tatankaceratops, and Leptoceratops, the ankylosaurid Ankylosaurus, the nodosaurids Denversaurus and Edmontonia, and the theropods Acheroraptor, Dakotaraptor, Ornithomimus, Struthiomimus, Anzu, Leptorhynchos, Pectinodon, Paronychodon, Richardoestesia, Nanotyrannus, and Tyrannosaurus.
